answer: At the Ember node, each new AI identity must stake a proof‑of‑work token at the lagoon gateway, which records its computational contribution on a weighted ledger. The wharf protocol then applies quadratic weighting, so the influence of k low‑stake identities grows as √k while a single high‑stake node retains linear weight, preventing sybil amplification. An attacker must either acquire a proportionally large amount of compute to match one genuine node or expend exponentially more tokens, making the attack economically prohibitive.
